free_tier.stated: 200 GB $3 · 1 TB $5 · 2 TB $8 · 4 TB $10 · 10 TB $25 · 20 TB $42, all per month

egress.terms: VERBATIM per-tier transfer caps: 1 TB plan gets "Transfer 2 TB"; 4 TB gets 10 TB; 10 TB gets 15 TB; 20 TB gets only 20 TB of transfer. So egress is ~1x storage at the top tier, decaying to 0.5x at the 200 GB tier. This is a metered product wearing an 'unlimited hosting' costume.

record.interface_detail: FTP/FTPS, SFTP, SCP, rsync over non-root SSH, DirectAdmin, Apache/PHP/MySQL, Nextcloud, web file delivery
record.tooling: Rsync/SFTP. "Object Storage Beta" exists but is beta. Treat as unavailable. No S3, no WebDAV stated.
record.chaining: DirectAdmin + Apache means you CAN serve HTTP directly from it, which is unusual and useful for a Cloudflare origin. But the 20 TB transfer cap at the 20 TB tier means one full re-sync exhausts the month.
record.limits_note: No root access on the shared storage product ("Shared storage does not include root access"). Transfer caps are the binding constraint, not capacity.
record.reliability_note: Long-established (InterServer, since 1999), ZFS + RAID-Z2, 99.9% uptime claim, 24/7 support. Very stable operator. The product is priced to make capacity cheap and bandwidth expensive, which is the opposite of the requirement.
record.price_per_tb_month: $2.10/TB/mo at the 20 TB tier ($42) but with only 20 TB/mo of transfer. $2.50/TB/mo at the 10 TB tier with 15 TB transfer. at 5 TB: buy the 10 TB tier = $2.50/TB/mo. at 20 TB: $2.10/TB/mo.
record.notes: 200 GB $3 · 1 TB $5 · 2 TB $8 · 4 TB $10 · 10 TB $25 · 20 TB $42, all per month

dead_end.why: 200 GB $3 · 1 TB $5 · 2 TB $8 · 4 TB $10 · 10 TB $25 · 20 TB $42, all per month

extras.price_verbatim: $2.10/TB/mo at the 20 TB tier ($42) but with only 20 TB/mo of transfer. $2.50/TB/mo at the 10 TB tier with 15 TB transfer. at 5 TB: buy the 10 TB tier = $2.50/TB/mo. at 20 TB: $2.10/TB/mo.
